questions.question: Which of the following is a large group of rock-forming silicate minerals that constitutes more than 50% of the Earth's crust and is widely used in the glass and ceramic industries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Feldspar.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Feldspar is the name of a large organization of **rock-forming silicate minerals** that make up over 50% of Earth's crust.
 
• They are discovered in **igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary rocks** in all components of the sector.
 
• Feldspar minerals have very **similar structures, chemical compositions, and physical properties.**
 
• **Silicate minerals** are rock-forming minerals made up of silicate groups. They are the largest and most important class of minerals and make up approximately 90 per cent of Earth's crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amphiboles** are **a major group of hydrous minerals that occur in a wide range of rock types**
 
• They occur predominantly in **metamorphic and igneous rocks** of the Earth's crust and upper mantle.
 
• Zeolites are **microporous, three-dimensional crystalline solids of aluminium silicate**.
 
• **Zeolites **have small openings of fixed size in them which allow small molecules to pass through them easily but larger molecules cannot pass through them; that is why they are sometimes called molecular sieves.
 
• **Pyroxenes** are **the most significant and abundant group of rock-forming ferromagnesian silicates**. 
 
• They are found in almost every variety of igneous rock and also occur in rocks of widely different compositions formed under conditions of regional and contact metamorphism.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the impeachment of the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 61.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 61 of the Constitution of India prescribes the procedure for the impeachment of the President.**
 
• When the President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by either House of Parliament.
 
• The president may also be removed before the expiry of the term through impeachment for violating the Constitution of India by the Parliament of India. 
 
• The process may start in either of the two houses of the parliament.
 
• The house initiates the process by leveling the charges against the president.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Process of Impeachment:**

 
 
• ​After the House of Representatives sends its articles of impeachment to the Senate, the Senate sits as a High Court of Impeachment to consider evidence, hear witnesses, and vote to acquit or convict the impeached official. A committee of representatives, called “managers,” act as prosecutors before the Senate.
 
 
 
• ​The President, Vice President, and all civil Officers of the United States shall be removed from Office on Impeachment for, and Conviction of, Treason, Bribery, or other high Crimes and Misdemeanors.
 
• Meaning of Impeachment:
 
• To charge with a crime or misconduct specifically: to charge (a public official) before a competent tribunal (as the U.S. Senate) with misconduct in office. Note: Impeachment is the first step in removing an officer from office.

questions.question: Which membrane-bound organelles, first discovered in 1857, are often referred to as the 'energy factories' of the cell because they are responsible for making adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the cell's main energy-carrying molecule?
questions.solution:
The corrrect answer is __**Mitochondria.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Mitochondria are frequently called the **“powerhouses” or “energy factories”** of a cell because they are incharge of making **adenosine triphosphate (ATP),** the cell's main energy-carrying molecule.
 
• Mitochondria, frequently referred to as the “powerhouses of the cell”, were first discovered in 1857 by physiologist **Albert von Kolliker**, and later coined** “bioblasts” (life germs) by Richard Altman in 1886.**
 
• **Mitochondria** are **membrane-bound cell organelles** that generate most of the chemical energy needed to power the cell's biochemical reactions.
 
• **Chemical energy produced by the mitochondria** is stored in a small molecule called** adenosine triphosphate (ATP).**

 [IMAGE: https://encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcSNemG45VCVcjwNf41WRaw7-QryDlGReNxX-FPBDk3NRQ&s] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The smooth endoplasmic reticulum functions in many metabolic processes. It **synthesizes lipids, phospholipids as in plasma membranes, and steroids**.
 
• A vacuole is **a membrane-bound cell organelle**. In animal cells, vacuoles are commonly small and help sequester waste products. In plant cells, vacuoles help maintain water balance. Sometimes a single vacuole can take up most of the interior space of the plant cell.
 
• A ribosome is **an intercellular structure made of both RNA and protein, and it is the site of protein synthesis in the cell**.

questions.question: Which enzyme is present in saliva?

__
 
• **Salivary amylase**** **is a glucose-polymer **cleavage enzyme** that is produced by the salivary glands.
 
• Amylases' main function is **to hydrolyze the glycosidic bonds in starch molecules, converting complex carbohydrates to simple sugars**.
 
• There are** three main classes of amylase enzymes; Alpha-, beta- and gamma-amylase**, and each act on **different parts of the carbohydrate molecule.**
 
• Amylases are used **in breadmaking** and to** break down complex sugars**, such as starch (found in flour), into simple sugars.

• **Trypsin** is **an enzyme that aids with digestion**. An enzyme is a protein that** speeds up a certain biochemical reaction.**
 
• An enzyme made in the stomach that **breaks down proteins in food during digestion**. Stomach acid changes a protein called **pepsinogen into pepsin.**

options.text: Protein translation, DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription
DNA Replication, m-RNA transcription, Protein translation
m-RNA transcription, Protein translation, DNA Replication
m-RNA transcription, DNA Replication, Protein translation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA Replication, mRNA transcription, Protein translation .**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **process by which DNA is copied to RNA** is called **transcription**, and that by which **RNA is used to produce proteins** is called **translation**.
 
• The major steps of transcription are **initiation, promoter clearance, elongation, and termination**.
 
• Essentially, what happens during transcription is that **an mRNA “copies down” the instructions for making a protein** from DNA.
 
• DNA replication is the **process by which the genome's DNA is copied** in cells.
 
• The process of translation can be seen as the **decoding of instructions for making proteins**, involving mRNA in transcription as well as tRNA.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d885884d008aeffbc804c583f27ef2d3ddc6211d497e2cec58bbdc89d987e9ed.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deoxyribonucleic acid (abbreviated DNA) is the **molecule that carries genetic information** for the development and functioning of an organism.
 
• Ribonucleic acid (abbreviated RNA) is a **nucleic acid present in all living cells** that has structural similarities to DNA.
 
• **Proteins** are made up of hundreds or thousands of **smaller units called amino acids**, which are **attached to one another in long chains**.
 
• Proteins are **20 different types of amino acids** that can be combined to make a protein.

questions.question: Match column A with column B. **Column-A** **Column-B** i. Powerhouse of a cell a.

options.text: i - a, ii - b, iii - c, iv - d
i - b, ii - a, iii - c, iv - d
i - d, ii - b, iii - c, iv - a
i - b, ii - a, iii - d, iv - c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i - b, ii - a, iii - d, iv - c.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The proteins synthesized by the proteins in mitochondria are utilized to generate ****adenosine triphosphate (ATP****) from the food.**
 
• This ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell, because of which the whole cell and body get energy.
 
 
• Thus, **mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cells.**
 
 
 
• **Chloroplast** is a plastid that is involved in the synthesis of carbohydrates through photosynthesis and is hence called the **kitchen of the cell.**
 
• Lysosomes are known **as suicide bags** of cell **because it contains digestive enzymes**. 
 
• The nucleus is like the **remote control centre of the cel**l. **It acts as the cell's brain by telling it what to do, how to grow, and when to reproduce**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In addition to producing energy, mitochondria perform some other functions for the cell including **cellular metabolism, the citric acid cycle, producing heat, controlling the concentration of calcium, and producing certain steroids**.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/19ff824a29bf438dd906e4e980ea9e725f31f22a5a8130b8ff6254a31c78305c.png] 

 
• Plastids are **pivotal subcellular organelles that have evolved to perform specialized functions in plant cells, including photosynthesis and the production and storage of metabolites**.
 
• A nucleus, as related to genomics, is **the membrane-enclosed organelle within a cell that contains the chromosomes**.
 
• Lysosomes are **membrane-enclosed organelles that contain an array of enzymes capable of breaking down all types of biological polymers—proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids**.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee Guru Keezhpadam Kumaran Nair was a dancer of which of the following classical dances of India?

questions.question: Which of the following is the birthplace of Tansen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gwalior.**__

__***Key Points__**

__
 
• Tansen born in **Behata or Gwalior **was an Indian musician and poet who was an important figure in the North Indian tradition of **Hindustani classical music.**
 
• Born in a Hindu brahmin family, he learnt and perfected his art in the northwest region of **modern ****Madhya Pradesh.**
 
• Tansen was a **composer, musician and vocalist**, to whom many compositions have been attributed in northern regions of the** Indian subcontinent.**
 
• He was also an **instrumentalist who popularized and improved musical instruments**. He is among the most influential personalities in the North Indian tradition of Indian classical music, called **Hindustani***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba0d6298f8d0b017375a723625442715d1692de6416277c09e51aae404a199b0.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The navratnas of Akbar's Court are **Abul Fazl, Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana, Birbal, Mulla Do-Piyaza Faizi, Raja Man Singh, Raja Todar Mal, Fakir Aziao-Din and Tansen.**
 
• **Abul Fazl, Akbar's friend **and counsellor, helped him frame the idea of** Sulh-i Kul **so that he could govern a society composed of many religions, cultures and castes.
 
• **Khanzada Mirza Khan Abdul Rahim, **generally known as simply Rahim and titled Khan-i-Khanan, was a poet who lived in India during the rule of Mughal emperor Akbar, who was his mentor.
 
• He was one of the nine main ministers in his court, known as the Navaratnas.
 
• Man Singh I, popularly known as **Mirza Raja Man Singh** was the **29th Kachwaha Rajput Raja of Amer, later known as Jaipur state, in Rajputana.**
